sources.title: Public Policy Immersion — reviewed policy course cards
sources.locator: Current curriculum table and complete public course popup opened from its exact code link.

scope: Twelve actual full public course cards; manual subject review is separate from runtime observations and does not certify degree completeness.

PUBL-530.name: Energy Policy
PUBL-530.description: Examines energy resources and technologies, their societal effects, and policies shaping energy development, emphasizing the United States within a global context.
notes: No prerequisite field is printed in the inspected card; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: The organizing work evaluates social impacts and public-policy choices for energy technology, rather than technical engineering design.

SOIS-333.name: Wicked Problems
SOIS-333.description: Uses whole-systems thinking, estimation, valuation and team case studies to investigate an open multidisciplinary problem.
SOIS-333.prerequisites: This class is restricted to undergraduate students with at least 3rd year standing.
notes: Four lecture contact hours are published separately from the three course credits.

category_review.rationale: The actual description defines broad problem-solving methods and a variable topical project without establishing a primary subject in this taxonomy.

PUBL-201.name: Ethics, Values & Public Policy
PUBL-201.description: Examines how values, norms and ethics shape policy choices, implementation and international differences, including science and technology issues.
notes: No prerequisite field is printed in the inspected card; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: Ethical reasoning, social values and their relationship to public decisions are the explicit organizing subject.

PUBL-210.name: Introduction to Qualitative Policy Analysis
PUBL-210.description: Develops qualitative social-research designs, data gathering, interpretation and inference using surveys, interviews and content analysis in policy cases.
notes: No prerequisite field is printed in the inspected card; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: The course explicitly centers qualitative social inquiry and interpretation for public policy; no primary mathematical or programming curriculum is stated.

PUBL-301.name: Public Policy Analysis
PUBL-301.description: Combines policy-process analysis with cost-benefit methods, sampling designs and decision trees applied to public decisions.
PUBL-301.prerequisites: Prerequisites: This class is restricted to students with at least 2nd year standing.

category_review.rationale: The description places emphasis on both policy-process interpretation and quantitative analysis, without establishing one as primary.

PUBL-302.name: Decision Analysis
PUBL-302.description: Introduces forecasting, risk analysis and multi-attribute decision methods, applying them to public-policy decisions.
PUBL-302.prerequisites: Prerequisites: This class is restricted to students with at least 2nd year standing.

category_review.rationale: The stated focus is decision-analysis methods, forecasting and risk tools; policy decisions supply the application domain.

PUBL-360.name: Social Policy and Inequity
PUBL-360.description: Evaluates welfare and inequity policies through justice, equality, fairness and care, emphasizing disadvantaged populations.
notes: May repeat for a different topic; the same topic may not be repeated.
No prerequisite field is printed in the inspected card; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: Ethical frameworks and the interpretation of social inequity are the substantive center.

PUBL-363.name: Cyber Security Policy and Law
PUBL-363.description: Examines nontechnical legal, political, economic and international-policy responses to cybersecurity threats.
notes: No prerequisite field is printed in the inspected card; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: The source expressly defines its focus as nontechnical laws and policy, rather than security infrastructure or software construction.

PUBL-510.name: Technological Innovation and Public Policy
PUBL-510.description: Examines models of technological innovation and government policies shaping economic and societal impacts across sectors.
notes: No prerequisite field is printed in the inspected card; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: Government choices, technology transfer and societal impacts organize the course; innovation models support this policy interpretation.

PUBL-515.name: Business and Public Policy
PUBL-515.description: Analyzes interactions among government interventions, businesses, markets, political participation and societal needs.
notes: No prerequisite field is printed in the inspected card; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: The full description organizes business-government relations around laws, policy participation and societal needs, rather than business operating practice.

PUBL-520.name: Information & Communications Policy
PUBL-520.description: Examines federal and international regulation of information technology, including privacy, speech, intellectual property, access and the Internet.
notes: No prerequisite field is printed in the inspected card; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: The substantive content is rights, regulation and public policy rather than networks or computing infrastructure.

PUBL-589.name: Topics in Public Policy
PUBL-589.description: Studies a variable public-policy problem; content and methods change by term.
notes: Published credit range: 1–4 credits. Scalar credit value remains null; three lecture contact hours do not establish three course credits.
No prerequisite field is printed in the inspected card; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: The inspected card confirms variable topics and methods but supplies no specific subject sufficient for a course-wide classification.
